2608.10807.title: Modelling Geographic Atrophy Progression using Implicit Neural Representations
2608.10807.paper_summary: Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) is the major cause of blindness in the Western world. Its late dry phase is characterised by irreversible atrophic areas, namely Geographic Atrophy (GA). Longitudinal Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF) image acquisitions are currently the main tool for assessing lesion growth over time at the image level. However, due to its highly individualised progression, the evolution of late AMD remains poorly understood. In this work, we propose using Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) to model GA progression at the individual level in a low-data setting. Our approach generates both FAF and GA segmentation at both past and future time points. Among the comparison models, our method achieves competitive segmentation quality across different scenarios, yielding the lowest Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for the GA lesion area and the highest DICE score, without sacrificing FAF image quality. The code is available at https://github.com/SimoneSarrocco/ga-progression-with-inrs.
2608.10807.paper_summary_zh: 年齡相關性黃斑變性（AMD）是西方世界失明的主要原因。其晚期乾性階段的特徵是不可逆的萎縮區域，即地理性萎縮（GA）。縱向眼底自體螢光（FAF）影像獲取目前是評估病變隨時間增長的主要工具。然而，由於其高度個體化的進展，晚期AMD的演變仍然不甚了解。在本研究中，我們提出使用隱式神經表示（INRs）在低數據環境中對GA進展進行個體層面的建模。我們的方法在過去和未來的時間點生成FAF和GA分割。在比較模型中，我們的方法在不同場景中實現了競爭性的分割質量，對於GA病變區域產生了最低的平均絕對誤差（MAE）和最高的DICE分數，且不犧牲FAF影像質量。代碼可在 https://github.com/SimoneSarrocco/ga-progression-with-inrs 獲得。
